description: A study of one street or highway corridor: what it does today, what it fails to do, what could be changed, and which changes to pursue first.
scope_notes: This is a standard-practice starting point — edit to your scope. Rename, delete and add records until the list matches the work your agency actually agreed to do.

Every date is calculated forward from the notice-to-proceed date you enter. The offsets are round numbers reflecting how this kind of work is usually sequenced — they are placeholders for a real schedule, not commitments.

It assumes a consultant-led study under a notice to proceed. An in-house study runs the same sequence without the procurement steps — change the anchor to the kickoff date and adjust the early offsets.

No jurisdiction is assumed. Review periods, required notices, hearings and the body that adopts the work are set where you are; none of them are stated here. Add the records your own process requires.
Nobody is assigned. Applying a template never puts a colleague's name on a deadline — assign the records yourself once the team is settled.

deliverables.title: Work plan, schedule and communication protocol
deliverables.summary: The agreed task list, schedule, meeting cadence and who speaks for which agency, confirmed after kickoff.

deliverables.title: Existing conditions and data summary
deliverables.summary: Traffic, transit, walking and cycling counts, collision history, land use and known constraints along the corridor, each with its source named.

deliverables.title: Corridor needs and opportunities memo
deliverables.summary: What the data and the community together say the corridor is failing to do, stated before any solution is proposed.

deliverables.title: Alternatives development and screening memo
deliverables.summary: Concepts developed against the agreed criteria, with the reasons any concept was screened out written down.

deliverables.title: Draft corridor study report
deliverables.summary: The complete draft assembled for technical and public review.

deliverables.title: Final corridor study report
deliverables.summary: The draft revised in response to comments, with the comment record attached.

deliverables.title: Implementation and phasing plan
deliverables.summary: A prioritized project list with planning-level cost estimates prepared by your team, sequenced into near, medium and long term.

milestones.title: Project kickoff meeting
milestones.summary: Scope, schedule, data sources and roles confirmed with everyone who has a part in the study.

milestones.title: Field data collection complete
milestones.summary: Counts, observations and inventory work finished so analysis can start from a settled dataset.

milestones.title: First public workshop — needs and opportunities
milestones.summary: The corridor's problems described publicly before alternatives exist, so input shapes them rather than reacting to them.

milestones.title: Technical advisory review of alternatives
milestones.summary: Partner agencies and internal reviewers see the alternatives before the draft is written.

milestones.title: Public review of the draft opens
milestones.summary: The draft is released for comment. Set the closing date to the period your agency has committed to.

milestones.title: Study accepted by the sponsoring body
milestones.summary: The decision that closes the study, by whichever body has that authority here.
